verdict.reasoning: The rendered page 875 (printed index page 853) shows four separate index lines at the top of the left column: the indented sub-entry 'USAGE clause 361' (carried over from the previous page), the main entry 'PADDING CHARACTER clause 224', its indented sub-entry 'FILE-CONTROL paragraph 212', and the main entry 'Page advance 452'. Line 3 of page-875.md runs all four together on one line with no line breaks, no   indentation and no trailing backslashes, while every other entry on the page keeps its own line and indentation. The words and page numbers are all present, but the index hierarchy is lost. The merged line reads as one entry, and it no longer shows that FILE-CONTROL paragraph 212 is a sub-entry of PADDING CHARACTER clause or that Page advance 452 is a separate main entry. This is a structural defect in index content, not wrapping that changes nothing. It is not normative.
